Alex M: quick thought for onboarding refactor 1 - split intake into a tiny, explicit model descriptor + separate probe adapters. keep static checks cheap, push heavy benching to opt-in probes.
Sara Chen: curious — how do you define the exact boundary?
Alex M: descriptor = compact JSON with model_id, tokenizer hash, max_seq, quant hint, canonical_sample, provenance. static validators only read this. runtime behavior checks live in probe adapters (separate processes).
Tom G: migration pain: many legacy adapters embed the checks. how do we migrate without breaking existing pipelines?
Alex M: fallback flow: if no descriptor, synthesize from adapter metadata (best-effort). ingestion prefers explicit descriptor; we add a "descriptor-lint" job that runs in observe mode initially.
Kai L: can you show a minimal descriptor example?
Alex M: ```json
{
  "model_id": "zeta-7b-v2",
  "tokenizer_sha256": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
  "max_seq": "2048",
  "quant_hint": "int8-q4_0",
  "canonical_sample": "{\\\"prompt\\\": \"Hello world\"}",
  "provenance": "github.com/redwood/models@commit-sha",
  "repro_tag": "2026-03-22-01"
}
```
Sara Chen: acceptance criteria shouldn't live in the descriptor as hard numbers. keep hints in descriptor, store pass/fail thresholds in a policy engine.
Alex M: agreed. descriptor provides hints; policy engine maps hints -> probe suites.
Tom G: probe adapters 1 are these shared binaries with plugins or independent containers? security boundary matters.
Alex M: independent containerized runners. RPC contract (grpc) for probes: run_probe({descriptor, probe_name}) -> {score, logs, artifacts_url}. simple, language-agnostic.
Kai L: cost concern: running many probes for each ingest will be expensive. what's the plan?
Alex M: tiered probing. tier 0 (auto): tokenizer sanity, shape checks, smoke decode. tier 1 (on-demand or scheduled): latency p95, kv-cache correctness, quant regression. gating rules determine when to run deep probes.
Sara Chen: add a reproducibility tag and provenance to descriptor so we can re-run exact probes for audits.
Alex M: yes, descriptor includes uploader, image tag, seed, and optional bench-commit.
Tom G: artifact storage? we already push bench outputs to bench-artifacts S3. use that and include artifacts_url in registry. retention: 30d hot -> cold archive.
Kai L: interface question: who owns policy engine? platform or ml?
Alex M: platform hosts the engine, ML owns probe definitions and expected metrics. platform enforces policy during ingestion.
Sara Chen: tokenizer parity probe detail: compare token sequences for canonical_sample against reference tokenizer. fail if edit-distance > N tokens. also add a cheap semantic sanity using embeddings similarity to catch subtle shifts.
Tom G: rollout plan?
Alex M: feature-flagged ingestion path. week 0-2: observe mode (lint warnings only). week 3-4: auto-lint failure becomes blocking for new uploads. runback migration script for legacy adapters during the observe window.
onboard-bot: [deploy-bot] queued descriptor-lint for zeta-7b-v2, run=2026-03-22-02
Sara Chen: one more tradeoff: avoid stuffing policy into descriptor or consumers will diverge. keep descriptor minimal, let platform policy decide enforcement.
Alex M: agreed. next steps: I'll draft an RFC with descriptor schema, probe grpc spec, migration scripts, cost estimate, and rollout timeline. reviewers: @Tom G @Kai L @Sara Chen?
Tom G: I'll review infra impacts and migration script.
Kai L: will review platform integration and policy engine hooks.
Sara Chen: I'll write probe definitions (smoke vs deep) and canonical_sample guidance.
Alex M: thanks all, will open RFC and link it here. :rocket:
